reason: E1 and E2 show elastic undulations at twin boundaries in pure Ni and CoCrFeMnNi, but only under external stress during deformation, not during thermal exposure or in the specific alloy. No evidence supports that these undulations promote precipitate nucleation, induce stress concentrations leading to failure, or that twin density reduction delays degradation. E3 is about a different alloy and deformation mechanism, providing no support.
premises: Twin boundaries in FCC HEAs produce nanoscale elastic field undulations with ~1–2 nm wavelength
These elastic undulations can serve as preferential nucleation sites for precipitates
Localized precipitate nucleation at twin boundaries induces stress concentrations that drive early crack initiation
Reducing twin density delays degradation by reducing preferential nucleation sites
The proposed mechanism applies to Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA at 750 °C in oxidizing/reducing gases
